verdict.rationale: Logseq documents page properties (e.g. `publish:: true`), block tagging (`#Page`) and simple `{{query}}` retrieval. A DB-version user reports that tagging blocks makes them typed things (project, author, quote). However, the first-party docs never describe typed property schemas or how tags and properties are queried consistently, and users say advanced queries are hard and poorly documented. missing for 10: first-party documentation of typed property definitions/schemas, documented property- and tag-based query retrieval, and evidence of consistent enforcement across notes.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can attach typed properties and tags to notes and use them consistently for organization and retrieval

citations.quote: Individual pages can be marked as public with the property `publish:: true`.
To convert this block to a page, simply tag the block with `#Page`.
Tagging blocks makes them typed things (project, author, quote).
Simple queries by using `{{query }}`, the format is something like this: {{query Something you're looking for}}
